title: Prefill-side microcache and tokenizer steering to reduce prefill stalls and kernel-switch overhead
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce prefill-side CPU and latency overhead for small-to-medium prompt workloads by introducing a session-local microcache for normalized token prefixes and a lightweight tokenizer steering hint to the kernel selector. This ticket focuses on prefill (ingest/prefill) path improvements — not downstream decode scheduling — but we will validate interactions with KV cache and decode lanes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end median prefill latency reduced by >=8% for the SmallPrompt benchmark on p4d-like instances with 8k prompt distribution. 2) 95th percentile tail for prefill CPU stall time reduced by >=15%. 3) No regression (>1%) in tokenization canonicalization correctness across existing tokenization unit tests and the expanded emoji/unicode suite. 4) Memory increase per session <= 128KB (configurable).
plan: 1) Implement a tiny session-local LRU (microcache) keyed by normalized-prefix-hash that caches: normalized bytes, tokenization hints (leading token length histogram), and a compact 'kernel_hint' bitmask. 2) Add a tokenizer fast-path that checks the microcache before full normalization/tokenization. 3) Expose the kernel_hint to the runtime's kernel-selection hot path via a compact enum (no cross-thread allocation). 4) Benchmark against current baseline, iterate on hash function and eviction policy. 5) Add tests and a feature flag to gate rollout.
benchmarks: Baseline: SmallPrompt suite (N=10k requests) on runtime-1.20: median prefill latency 12.2ms, P95 45ms, prefill CPU stall median 3.1ms. Experiment phase A (microcache + ascii-fastpath): median 10.9ms (-10.7%), P95 39ms (-13.3%), stall median 2.5ms (-19.4%). Phase B (add kernel_hint steering): median 10.6ms (-13.1%), P95 36ms (-20%), observed improved kernel hot-hit rate from 78% -> 89% for short-prefix kernels.
decisions: - Use a 64-bit xxhash keyed by normalized bytes as microcache key to minimize collision risk. - Cache stores normalized bytes up to 256 bytes and token-hint bitmap; larger prefixes fall back to full normalize. - Kernel hint is an enum: SHORT_SEQ_OPT | MEDIUM_SEQ_OPT | LONG_SEQ_FALLBACK. - Microcache is per-session, not global, to avoid cross-session eviction churn and reduce synchronization.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduced redundant normalization and fewer kernel switches during prefill, measurable latency/cpu wins. Cons: modest per-session memory increase, additional complexity in tokenizer hotpath, possible increased branch mispredictions in worst-case. Risk of stale hints if upstream normalization logic changes — tests and versioned cache keys added to mitigate.
open_questions: - Best eviction policy: LRU vs clock? We prototyped LRU; clock may be cheaper — need microbench. - Interaction with shared KV prefill cache: should the microcache consult global cache first? Current plan: check session microcache, then global KV-prefill. - Should kernel_hint be surfaced to requester-level tracing for cost attribution? Product asked to consider this.
next_steps: 1) Complete unit and integration tests (Marco). 2) Run a 3-day canary on dedicated staging pool (runtime-1.21 canary) and collect per-model kernel hit metrics (Riley). 3) Add flag for 'microcache-size' and 'enable-kernel-hint' to rollout via console. 4) Prepare PRD and rollout playbook for cases where memory footprint exceeds budget (Asha).
